issues.remediation: Migrate the legacy .NET Framework WPF project file to SDK-style and retarget to net8.0-windows. Replace TargetFrameworkVersion with TargetFramework, add UseWPF, and remove legacy bootstrapper/publish settings that are specific to .NET Framework.
issues.title: Project targets .NET Framework 4.8 instead of .NET 8
issues.description: The main project file is a legacy non-SDK-style .csproj targeting .NET Framework 4.8. .NET 8 requires SDK-style project configuration and a Windows-specific target framework for WPF applications.
issues.recommendation: Convert the project to SDK-style and use <TargetFramework>net8.0-windows</TargetFramework> with <UseWPF>true</UseWPF>. Re-evaluate legacy properties such as ProjectTypeGuids, bootstrapper packages, ClickOnce publish metadata, and explicit framework assembly references.
issues.impact: The application cannot build or run on .NET 8 until the project system is migrated.

issues.remediation: Replace .NET Framework runtime configuration with .NET 8-compatible application settings. Remove supportedRuntime and assemblyBinding redirects from App.config, and move required settings to appsettings.json or a simplified runtime config strategy appropriate for desktop .NET 8 apps.
issues.title: App.config contains .NET Framework-only runtime settings
issues.description: The application configuration declares a .NET Framework runtime SKU and assembly binding redirects. These settings are not used the same way in .NET 8 and indicate a runtime model that is incompatible with the target platform.
issues.recommendation: Remove supportedRuntime and bindingRedirect sections during migration. Keep only settings that are still needed, and migrate user/application settings to a .NET 8-compatible configuration approach.
issues.impact: Runtime configuration will not map cleanly to .NET 8 and can hide dependency resolution problems during migration.

issues.remediation: Replace packages.config and explicit assembly HintPath references with SDK-style PackageReference entries. Reassess each package for .NET 8 compatibility and update to supported versions.
issues.title: Legacy packages.config-based dependency management blocks .NET 8 migration
issues.description: The project uses packages.config and explicit assembly references from the packages folder. .NET 8 migrations should use PackageReference in an SDK-style project, and several current references are tied to .NET Framework-targeted assets.
issues.recommendation: Migrate all NuGet dependencies to PackageReference and validate package support for net8.0-windows. Remove direct HintPath references from the project file.
issues.impact: Package restore and dependency resolution will remain tied to .NET Framework conventions and may fail or select incompatible assets on .NET 8.

issues.remediation: Replace AForge/AForge.Video/AForge.Video.DirectShow with a camera/video library that supports modern .NET, or isolate camera capture behind an abstraction and port to a supported package.
issues.title: AForge camera stack is not a safe .NET 8 dependency choice
issues.description: The project references legacy AForge packages and uses AForge video APIs in the ID generation workflow. These libraries are historically tied to older .NET Framework scenarios and are a common migration blocker for .NET 6+ and .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Evaluate supported alternatives such as OpenCvSharp-based capture, DirectShow-compatible maintained wrappers, or MediaCapture abstractions that support current .NET Windows desktop targets.
issues.impact: Camera capture functionality may fail to compile or behave unpredictably after migration.

issues.remediation: Remove unsupported framework assemblies and replace them with supported APIs or packages. In particular, eliminate System.Web and System.Data.OracleClient references unless there is verified code and package support for a replacement.
issues.title: Project references obsolete or unsupported framework assemblies for .NET 8
issues.description: The project file includes framework assembly references that do not belong in a .NET 8 WPF desktop application. System.Web is not part of .NET 8 desktop apps, and System.Data.OracleClient is obsolete and unavailable in modern .NET.
issues.recommendation: Remove these references during SDK-style migration. If Oracle access is required, use Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core or another supported provider. Replace any System.Web usage with modern equivalents if present.
issues.impact: The project will not compile on .NET 8 with unsupported framework assembly references retained.

issues.remediation: Review System.Drawing usage and move image-processing code to WPF-native imaging APIs or a supported cross-platform/Windows-specific graphics library. Avoid relying on System.Drawing.Common behavior in .NET 8.
issues.title: System.Drawing.Common usage is risky for .NET 8 migration
issues.description: The project references System.Drawing.Common and uses System.Drawing types in multiple files. System.Drawing.Common has important support limitations in modern .NET and is a frequent migration issue, especially outside tightly controlled Windows-only scenarios.
issues.recommendation: For WPF, prefer BitmapSource, RenderTargetBitmap, BitmapImage, and related imaging APIs. Where drawing primitives are required, evaluate SkiaSharp or another supported library.
issues.impact: Image capture, rendering, or printing code may require refactoring to remain stable on .NET 8.

issues.remediation: When converting to SDK-style, explicitly configure modern compiler defaults such as ImplicitUsings and Nullable, then address resulting warnings incrementally.
issues.title: Project lacks .NET 8 language feature configuration
issues.description: The current legacy project file does not define ImplicitUsings or Nullable settings. While not a hard blocker by itself, this leaves the migrated project without explicit modern compiler behavior and increases migration uncertainty.
issues.recommendation: After SDK-style migration, add <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings> and decide whether to use <Nullable>enable</Nullable> immediately or phase it in with warnings managed over time.
issues.impact: The migrated project may miss standard .NET 8 conventions and produce avoidable maintenance issues.

issues.remediation: Review local time logging and decide whether timestamps should use DateTimeOffset.Now or UTC-based logging for consistent behavior after migration.
issues.title: DateTime.Now usage should be reviewed during .NET 8 migration
issues.description: The rules require review of DateTime handling. The logger uses DateTime.Now, which is not a direct blocker but should be validated for timezone correctness and consistency during modernization.
issues.recommendation: Prefer DateTimeOffset.Now for local timestamps with offset information, or DateTimeOffset.UtcNow if centralized log correlation is required.
issues.impact: Timestamp interpretation may become inconsistent across environments or future integrations.

issues.remediation: Document the required upgrade path instead of attempting an in-place framework switch. This application should move from .NET Framework WPF to net8.0-windows through project conversion and dependency validation.
issues.title: Direct in-place upgrade path from .NET Framework 4.8 to .NET 8 is not represented in the current solution
issues.description: The solution is a classic .NET Framework WPF application with legacy project system metadata, bootstrapper packages, and framework-era configuration. This indicates a staged migration is required rather than a simple target version edit.
issues.recommendation: Plan a staged migration: convert project format, migrate package management, remove framework-only runtime config, replace unsupported dependencies, then validate WPF-specific behavior on net8.0-windows.
issues.impact: Attempting a direct retarget without staged remediation is likely to fail and create cascading compatibility issues.

recommendations.recommendation: Convert the WPF project to SDK-style and retarget to net8.0-windows with UseWPF enabled before addressing package and code-level issues.
Replace packages.config with PackageReference and validate every dependency for .NET 8 Windows desktop compatibility, especially AForge and System.Drawing-related usage.
Remove .NET Framework runtime declarations and binding redirects from App.config, preserving only settings that are still needed in a .NET 8 desktop configuration model.
Review System.Drawing and DateTime usage and refactor to WPF-native imaging and DateTimeOffset-based logging where appropriate.
